transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sarah (NorthPoint Head of Platform), Devon (NorthPoint ML Eng), Marta (CTO), Evan (SRE)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to 45 mins ish, quick agenda — bench readout, latency and throughput deltas vs their incumbent, routing questions and then next steps.
[00:18] Sarah: Great, thanks. Devon and Evan are on for the numbers, Marta's on briefly to listen.
[00:25] Devon: hey hi, quick note — we've been running the baseline traces against IncumbentAI for two weeks, avg payload is around 6k tokens but we have a long tail up to 30k for a subset of requests.
[00:38] Diego: good, that's exactly what we wanted to stress. we brought priya to show the new quantize-config we tried this sprint.
[00:45] Priya: yeah so we ran redwood compiled kernels with int4-ish quant and our batching set to prefix-aware continuous batching, also enabled KV cache warmup for repeated sessions. results below.
[00:58] [00:58] Devon: can you just say int4-ish, like are you calling it q4 or q4_0?
[01:03] Priya: it's closer to q4_0 but with our per-layer scaling, so some layers are lighter quant. transcription note: sometimes model names come out weird in the transcript, we used the S-7B-v2-ish variant.
[01:20] [01:20] Diego: ok bench numbers: cold-start p50 for the incumbent on the 6k median payload was ~310ms, p95 ~720ms; on Redwood hosted variant p50 was 260ms, p95 580ms. for 30k tails, incumbent p50 1.9s p95 4.6s; Redwood p50 1.5s p95 3.9s. these are single-replica numbers, no dedicated slots.
[01:50] Devon: those deltas look promising but the cost numbers we saw last week for Redwood were... higher for high-concurrency bursts?
[01:58] Maya: yep that's expected without batching and caching tuned for their traffic. we recommended continuous batching + prefix cache which reduces per-token GPU time. priya, quick why does the p95 improve on your q4 run?
[02:12] Priya: quant reduces kernel time and memory bandwidth so the long-sequence passes are faster, but there's a small quality delta — in our eval set we saw token accuracy drop ~0.7% on the 30k prompts.
[02:25] Devon: 0.7% might be fine for internal search, but not for clinical summaries. any way to keep quality?
[02:31] Priya: yes — hybrid routing: keep critical workflows on fp16 or q8 and route bulk/background on q4. also adjust thresholding on the reranker to catch regressions.
[02:42] Sarah: can you clarify routing options — are we doing region fallback or model variant fallback? we can't send PHI to a public endpoint for some flows.
[02:50] Diego: good point — you have three levers: region routing (stay in us-east VPC), capacity tier routing (dedicated vs hosted), and model variant routing (fp16 vs q4). for PHI flows we'd recommend dedicated slots in your VPC/private deployment with KMS integration.
[03:08] Evan: what about audit logs and SOC2 — our security team will ask for logs at token level or at least request-level traces.
[03:15] Maya: Redwood provides audit logs and an exports pipeline; Private deployment includes full audit trails and KMS/HSM key support. we can share SOC2 pak plus a design doc.
[03:25] Marta: high level question — on the long tail, is the bottleneck GPU compute or NVMe/IO?
[03:31] Diego: mostly compute and kv cache misses. the 30k sequences amplify KV cache pressure and memory movement; our runtime reduces cache misses by prefetching and chunked KV streaming but there are still hits under extreme concurrency.
[03:46] Devon: we noticed bigger degradation when concurrency jumped above 120 req/s to the same model.
[03:51] Priya: yes, tail latency is sensitive to concurrency. our next test should simulate their burst pattern — 30s ramp to 200rps, hold 2 minutes, then drop. that will surface the queuing effects and batching efficiency.
[04:08] Maya: agreed — action: Diego to run that burst profile head-to-head against IncumbentAI with these routing configs: (1) Redwood hosted default, (2) Redwood hosted + q4 with hybrid routing, (3) Redwood dedicated slots with prewarmed cache.
[04:21] Devon: do you want traces? we can provide the 24h traffic trace and also a synthetic generator for burst shape.
[04:26] Diego: yes please, Sarah if you can upload to the shared S3 bucket that we gave last sprint.
[04:31] Sarah: will do by EOD Friday.
[04:33] [04:33] Evan: small interruption — how do you measure p95 when streaming responses? we have partial streaming clients.
[04:39] Priya: we capture time-to-first-token and last-token; p95 here is last-token latency measured end-to-end. streaming helps perceived latency but doesn't reduce cost unless you cut generation length.
[04:50] Devon: on cost, your hosting pricing for high memory models had a per-token uplift; can you show impact for q4 vs fp16 in rough $/1M tokens?
[04:58] Maya: quick numbers now: fp16 baseline $X per 1M tokens (we'll send exact sheet), q4 reduces GPU token time by ~30-35% so cost also drops ~25-30% depending on batch hit rate. but if you need quality SLAs, hybrid routing mix matters.
[05:17] Marta: is there any other vendor lock risk with your compiled kernel approach? we want portability.
[05:22] Diego: kernels are tuned but we support standard model formats and export; customers can run our runtime on-prem in Private mode. the compiled kernel is our optimization layer but we don't prevent model export.
[05:34] Devon: interesting — one thing we observed: incumbent does automatic prefix caching but their cache invalidation is weird, sometimes stale outputs. how's your cache invalidation?
[05:44] Priya: our prefix/KV cache uses request fingerprinting and TTLs, plus a manual invalidation API. we've seen improved hit rates with session affinity. caveat: privacy-sensitive payloads should be stored only in Private deployment if needed.
[06:00] Sarah: ok can you summarize the top three risks we should watch during the pilot?
[06:05] Diego: (1) quality regression under q4 on clinical summaries, (2) burst tail latency if cache warmup isn't seeded, (3) network egress/region constraints for PHI flows.
[06:15] Devon: agree, add (4) cost unpredictability during unexpected traffic spikes.
[06:20] Maya: action items and owners — we'll write them up, but quick recap: Diego runs head-to-head burst test, Maya sends pricing & dedicated slot options, NorthPoint to upload traces.
[06:31] Sarah: timeline — can we aim to have the head-to-head results w/ logs by next sync on 2027-10-19?
[06:36] Maya: yes that's doable, Diego?
[06:38] Diego: yes, I'll run tests early next week and share artifacts.
[06:42] [06:42] Priya: one final note — for the clinical pipelines, we recommend starting hybrid: route real-time summaries to fp16, batch background enrichment on q4 with an additional reranker. that keeps SLA while lowering unit cost.
[06:56] Marta: thanks all, that sounds like a reasonable compromise.
[07:00] Maya: perfect. we'll follow up with the pricing sheet and the SOC2 + private deployment docs. Anyone else?
[07:07] Devon: no, thanks.
[07:09] Sarah: thanks team.
[07:12] Maya: end.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker attribution errors (Speaker 2 vs Diego), some acronyms mis-typed (KV cahce), model name fuzzy (S-7B-v2-ish).
